calls.body: The Panthers’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Blue Jackets’ kill is one of the worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Blue Jackets more than most.

calls.head: Patience vs. Spray-and-pray
calls.body: The Blue Jackets wait for good looks, but the Panthers settle for hopeful ones. Columbus is near the top of the league for shot quality, and Florida is one of the worst. The more dangerous chances should be the Blue Jackets’.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Bennett has two goals as the Panthers beat the Blue Jackets
paras: Sam Bennett and Lars Eller scored a little over two minutes apart early in the second to put the Panthers up 2-0. Ivan Provorov got the Blue Jackets on the board with 19 seconds left in the period, but they got no closer. Bennett scored again with less than six minutes left to make it 3-1 for the Cats. Sam Reinhart added an empty-net goal with a little over two minutes left to make it 4-1.
The chances were closer than the score. Jacob Markström made 38 saves for the Panthers, and Cam Talbot stopped 25 of 28 at the other end.
Erik Gudbranson and Brady Tkachuk picked up ten-minute misconducts. The Panthers moved to 10-7-2, fifth in the Atlantic, while the Blue Jackets fell to 7-9-0, seventh in the Metropolitan.
